newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's unions, employers sign final labour deal.
newsitem.headline: Spain's unions, employers sign final labour deal.

text.p: Spain's unions and employers signed a final deal on labour reforms on Monday, designed to liberalise one of Europe's most rigid jobs markets.
The two sides sealed their accord after their respective executive bodies approved the deal earlier this month.
It is now up to the government to convert the proposed reforms on contracts, dismissals and collective bargaining into legislation.

"Today is a good day for workers, especially those who lack work or who are working under precarious conditions," Antonio Gutierrez, secretary general of the Workers' Commission Union (CCOO) said after signing the deal.

The government hopes the reforms will go part of the way toward suppressing Spain's steep unemployment -- the highest in Europe at just under 22 percent -- and preparing the economy for European Monetary Union.

The key feature of the accord is a package of contracts aimed at providing more stability in the labour market and encouraging employers to take on staff. The centrepiece is a permanent contract which allows for cheaper severance pay -- a key demand of employers.
"This agreement is not a summary of general objectives, it includes concrete proposals," Candido Mendez, Secretary General of the General Workers' Union (UGT) said.

After months of intense talks, unions and employers reached a preliminary agreement in March which provided the foundations for a final accord. The two sides then revealed the details of their deal in early April.
